stem:
Rina notices that cooked spinach is softer and less bright green than raw spinach.

What is the best conclusion about cooking and nutrients?

options.text: Cooking heat destroys the minerals in the spinach, so it has no minerals left.
Cooking can change colour and texture and may reduce some nutrients such as vitamin C.
Cooked spinach contains no nutrients at all.
The duller colour proves that all of the vitamin C has been lost.

teacher.key_rationale: Cooking can soften vegetables and dull colour, and some nutrients such as vitamin C may be reduced; minerals are not simply destroyed, nutrients are not all gone, and colour alone does not prove vitamin C loss.
